title: add vpc control plane terraform + private-installer multi-az peering route53
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Customers deploying Redwood Private in multi-AZ AWS environments have requested a reproducible Terraform module + installer integration that provisions the VPC control plane (subnets, interface endpoints, security groups), cross-account peering, and Route53 private hosted zone peering/records as part of the private-installer flow. This PR bundles: 1) a reusable Terraform module for 'vpc-control-plane' with explicit support for multi-az subnets, interface endpoints (SSM, KMS, ECR, S3), and security group policies tuned for control plane traffic; 2) installer wiring (private-installer) to call the module via the Terraform wrapper and expose configuration flags; 3) Helm chart adjustments to accept the control plane networking outputs (peer VPC IDs, route53 delegation records) and configure ServiceAccount endpoints; 4) upgrade/rollback hooks that add safe migration steps for existing single-AZ installations to join a multi-AZ peering topology; and 5) docs and terratest coverage. The description below is a single continuous narrative that includes checklist items, motivation, and references. Motivation: enable our enterprise customers to provision an isolated control plane VPC with opinionated defaults (CIDR allocation, NAT configuration, security groups) and managed DNS peering (Route53) so that Private control plane services can resolve and route to customer workloads while preserving least-privilege networking. Design highlights: - Terraform module inputs: vpc_cidr, azs, public/private subnet sizing, interface_endpoints list, cross_account_peers (list of account ids and VPC ids), route53_hosted_zone_id, route53_peering_options. - Outputs exported for the installer: control_plane_vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, interface_endpoint_ids, control_plane_sg_id, route53_vpc_association_id. - Security groups: allow only specific control-plane ports (8443, 8080 for health/proxy, 22 restricted to bastion CIDRs), restrict cross-account peer traffic via explicit ingress rules, and documented justification for ephemeral CIDR allowances used for bootstrap. - Route53: create private hosted zone associations and shared delegations where requested; support cross-account zone association flow with prerequisite IAM role pattern documented in docs. - Upgrade path: when detecting an existing single-AZ control plane, installer will create new subnets in additional AZs, provision peering but keep traffic routed to primary AZ until canary validators pass; rollback will revert peering and remove newly-created subnets if canary fails. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module added: terraform/modules/vpc-control-plane (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, README.md) - [x] private-installer: call module and expose CLI flags (installer/aws/provisioner.go) - [x] terratest: tests/integration/vpc_control_plane_test.go - [x] helm/redwood-private: values schema extended and templates updated for new DNS/peering outputs - [x] docs: docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md with step-by-step and security considerations - [x] e2e: smoke test in perf-canary to validate cross-account peering. Related work: Linear ENG-2048 (multi-AZ control plane), ENG-1987 (private-installer terraform refactor), PM-112 (customer request: ACME Corp multi-az). Implementation notes: the module follows our existing terraform styleguide (module inputs are intentionally opinionated), uses dynamic blocks to create interface endpoints based on the interface_endpoints input, and includes tags and cost-center metadata. The installer validates required IAM roles for cross-account associations and will abort with an actionable error message if the role is missing. Rollback strategy: terraform destroy of the newly-created module state is run in a controlled step; before destroy we attempt to drain control-plane connections and create a temporary DNS failover record to the old primary endpoint. Testing: added terratest cases that run in a sandbox account and validate security group rules, endpoint reachability, and route53 associations. CI: terratest is marked as integration and runs on the integration runner with restricted concurrency. Security review: security@redwood signoff received for SG rules and least-privilege IAM patterns. See the files_changed list for areas to review; when reviewing focus on the upgrade hooks and the interface endpoint naming so we can avoid collisions in shared accounts. Links: docs/private/vpc-control-plane.md, Linear ENG-2048. This PR is intentionally large; consider reviewing by component (terraform module, installer wiring, helm changes, docs).
